# Implementation Plan: Durable Mailbox + Channel Wake (D-002)

> Seeded from brainstorm: `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/brainstorms/async-events-design/selected-direction.md` (direction D-002, scope-narrowed by operator decision 2026-06-02).
> Northstar / longer-horizon design — long-poll, generic producer hub, app-server `thread/subscribeEvents`, agent-comms Scope A, multi-session per-subscription routing — is **explicitly out of scope** and tracked separately under `async-events-northstar-architecture`.

## Overview

Land a documented **"Durable mailbox + channel wake"** architectural pattern and ONE reference implementation that proves it end-to-end for **agent-comms Scope B** (same-daemon cross-session messaging).

The pattern says: the durable filesystem mailbox is the **source of truth** for messages; the just-shipped MCP-notification consumer (`packages/happy-cli/src/codex/mcpNotificationConsumer.ts`) is used as the **pending-mail wake signal only**; missed wakes are harmless because the consumer-side re-reads the inbox on startup. Two vitest fixtures pin the contract: a happy-path two-session round-trip, and a missed-wake recovery scenario where the receiver is killed and restarted while a message is in-flight.

The implementation is TypeScript-only inside `packages/happy-cli/`. **ZERO `codex/` submodule changes** are required — the just-shipped Stage A `EventMsg::McpServerNotification` plus the in-process Option B consumer are sufficient surfaces, and keeping the work out of `codex/` minimizes upstream-rebase conflict surface per `packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md` § "Codex Submodule Edits (minimize conflict surface)".

The deliverable plays a dual role: it ships a concrete primitive (agent-comms Scope B) AND it codifies the answer to a broader open question — for a hypothetical codex-engine port of the `crews` plugin, channels are the wake hint, the filesystem mailbox is the durable substrate, and channels-native crews storage is rejected.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

The just-shipped Stage A + Option B layers (consumer side built, producer side absent) live entirely in `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/`:

- **`mcpNotificationConsumer.ts:1-185`** — `createMcpNotificationConsumer<TMode>(opts)` returns `{ handle(msg), dispose() }`. `handle()` is invoked for every codex event. It short-circuits when `routing.enabled === false` (`:120-122`), only acts on `mcp_server_notification` + `mcp_sampling_request` (`:165-177`), and pushes prompts onto the existing `MessageQueue2` debounced by `${server}|${uri ?? kind}` (`:96-104, :106-118`).
- **`mcpNotificationRouting.ts:1-291`** — fixed 7-kind whitelist (`progress, cancelled, resource_updated, resource_list_changed, tool_list_changed, prompt_list_changed, logging_message`). `RouteAction` = `display-only` | `prompt-queue { template, debounceMs? }`. Default-off when settings field absent. `resource_updated` ships with a default `prompt-queue` action and **250ms debounce**.
- **`runCodex.ts:286-305, 745-755`** — the consumer is constructed after `MessageQueue2` and called first in the `client.setEventHandler(...)` chain. The missed-wake recovery wiring lands in the same neighborhood as the consumer construction, but the recovery logic itself lives behind an exported `agentComms/recovery.ts` helper so tests can exercise it without booting the full `runCodex` harness.

The producer-side stdio MCP bridge that the producer wake will plug into:

- **`happyMcpStdioBridge.ts:1-105`** — minimal stdio MCP server, only `change_title` tool today. Per-Codex-session lifetime. Uses `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.25.3`; high-level `McpServer` exposes `.server.sendResourceUpdated({ uri })` for arbitrary `resource_updated` emission.

Daemon control plane already exists and is the natural site for the same-daemon send hop:

- **`daemon/controlServer.ts`** — local HTTP control server with `/session-started`, `/list`, `/spawn-session`, `/stop-session` etc.
- **`daemon/controlClient.ts`** — posts to the daemon control server on `127.0.0.1` without per-request capability auth; the `X-Loopback-Capability` pattern in `daemonClient.ts:114-121` belongs to the separate embedded loopback listener, not this control port.
- **`daemon/run.ts`** — tracks live + persisted sessions; the new route looks up the target session against tracked state.

Codex `multi_agents_v2` was evaluated per the brainstorm's disconfirming observation #1 ("the existing multi_agents_v2 mailbox may already be the right durable substrate") and rejected as the durable substrate: `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/core/src/session/input_queue.rs` stores mailbox notifications in an in-memory `watch::Sender<()>` / `watch::Receiver<()>` pair and pending mails in an in-memory `VecDeque<InterAgentCommunication>`. It cannot survive a daemon restart, so it refutes the disconfirming observation for this Scope B durability requirement; the filesystem inbox remains required.

Existing related test pattern (the missed-wake fixture borrows shape from):

- **`runCodex.mcpNotifications.test.ts`** — injects synthetic events into the consumer + asserts routing into a fake `MessageQueue2`. The new `scopeB.test.ts` extends this pattern to two simulated sessions + filesystem inbox + producer emit.

### Technical Constraints

| Constraint | Reason |
|---|---|
| **TypeScript only inside `packages/happy-cli/`** | Brainstorm criterion; matches Option B's already-shipped consumer being TS. |
| **ZERO `codex/` submodule edits** | Brainstorm criterion + `packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md` § "Codex Submodule Edits"; every codex edit costs subtree-pull conflict surface. |
| **Same-daemon only** | Brainstorm out-of-scope: cross-machine fan-out is Scope A (blocked on transport-policy decision). |
| **Between-turns delivery only** | Existing channels + codex mailbox semantics; mid-turn preemption is northstar territory. |
| **Unknown MCP notification kinds are dropped** | `mcpNotificationConsumer.ts:128-130` enforces the 7-kind whitelist. We MUST use one of the existing kinds — picking `resource_updated` with a real `file://` URI for the inbox file. |
| **No live routing reload** | `runCodex.ts:286-295` loads settings ONCE. "Routing re-enabled" mid-process means restart. So missed-wake recovery is **at startup only** in v1. |
| **Bridge is per-Codex-session** | Session A's bridge cannot push notifications into session B's bridge. **B's own bridge must watch B's inbox directory**, filter for `mailbox.json`, and emit `resources/updated` from inside B's process. The cross-session hop goes through the filesystem inbox (write by A, watched by B). |
| **Codex `multi_agents_v2` mailbox was evaluated and rejected as the durable substrate** | Per the brainstorm's disconfirming observation #1, `core/src/session/input_queue.rs` was checked and found to use an in-memory `watch::Receiver<()>` / `VecDeque<InterAgentCommunication>` only. It cannot survive daemon restart, so it refutes the observation for Scope B durability; the filesystem inbox is required. |
| **Producer-side MCP server lifetime is an INPUT, not solved** | `codex-app-server-idle-timeout` task wants the app-server to outlive foreground clients; this design surfaces that as an input note in §"Risk Areas" and the pattern doc, doesn't try to resolve. |
| **No fake URIs (Copilot research)** | Prefer real `file:///<absolute-path-to-mailbox.json>` over sentinel `agent-comms://...`. MCP-spec-strict + matches existing `resource_updated` defaults. |

## Approach

### Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────────────────┐         ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Session A (codex client + bridge)  │         │ Session B (codex client + bridge)  │
│                                    │         │                                    │
│  call happy-mcp.agent_comms.send   │         │   bridge fs.watch(<B inbox dir>)   │
│    bridge tool → controlClient     │         │           │                        │
│    POST /agent-comms/send (daemon) │         │           │                        │
│           │                        │         │           │  change event          │
└───────────┼────────────────────────┘         │           ▼                        │
            │                                  │   sendResourceUpdated(             │
            ▼                                  │     uri=file:///<B inbox>)         │
   ┌────────────────────────────────┐          │           │                        │
   │ daemon controlServer           │          │           ▼                        │
   │   POST /agent-comms/send       │          │   codex event:                     │
   │   → write to <B inbox> dir     │          │     mcp_server_notification        │
   │     via mailbox.appendMessage  │          │       kind=resource_updated        │
   └────────────────────────────────┘          │           │                        │
                                               │           ▼                        │
                                               │   mcpNotificationConsumer.handle() │
                                               │           │                        │
                                               │           ▼                        │
                                               │   MessageQueue2.push(              │
                                               │     "[agent-comms] pending mail")  │
                                               │           │                        │
                                               │           ▼ next turn boundary     │
                                               │   B reads agent-comms MCP resource │
                                               │           │                        │
                                               │           ▼                        │
                                               │   bridge read callback drains:     │
                                               │     readPending → return entries → │
                                               │     markConsumed(uptoSeq)          │
                                               └────────────────────────────────────┘

Filesystem source of truth:
  <happyHomeDir>/agent-comms/inboxes/<sessionId>/mailbox.json   (current pending + cursor)
  <happyHomeDir>/agent-comms/inboxes/<sessionId>/history.jsonl  (append-only audit)
```

**Four primitives, one shared substrate:**

1. **Mailbox storage** (`agentComms/mailbox.ts`) — append, read-pending(sinceSeq), mark-consumed(uptoSeq). Atomic JSON write via `writeJsonAtomically` from `@slopus/happy-wire/node`; history append uses raw fd `appendFile` with newline. Borrows the crews-plugin algorithmic shape WITHOUT depending on the plugin (which is CJS + in a sibling submodule).
2. **Daemon hop** (`daemon/controlServer.ts` POST `/agent-comms/send`) — the Codex-facing entrypoint is the sender's stdio MCP bridge tool `agent_comms.send`, which delegates to `controlClient.sendAgentMessage(...)`; that helper posts to the sender's own local daemon. The daemon validates target against tracked sessions + writes to target's inbox file. This keeps cross-session writes serialized through one process (the daemon) and avoids two-writer races on the inbox file.
3. **Producer wake** (in `happyMcpStdioBridge.ts`) — per-session bridge calls `mailbox.ensureInbox(currentSessionId)`, registers the `agent_comms.send` MCP tool, then `fs.watch`es its OWN inbox directory and filters `change`/`rename` events to `mailbox.json`; matching events emit `resource_updated` (URI = `file:///<absolute-path-to-mailbox.json>`). Directory watching avoids the nonexistent-file startup failure and survives atomic temp-write + rename replacement of `mailbox.json`. The just-shipped consumer routes this notification into `MessageQueue2`.
4. **Receiver drain** (also in `happyMcpStdioBridge.ts`) — the registered `agent-comms` MCP resource has an explicit read callback that calls `mailbox.readPending(currentSessionId)`, returns the pending entries to the receiver, and only then calls `mailbox.markConsumed(currentSessionId, uptoSeq)`. Wake enqueue paths MUST NOT mark entries consumed; the cursor advances only after this read/drain path has handed the entries to Codex.

**Required `mcpNotificationRouting` config** — no code changes are made to `mcpNotificationRouting.ts`, so the human-readable wake string comes from settings. The Happy stdio bridge is registered in `runCodex.ts` as MCP server key `happy`; therefore users/tests that want the agent-comms wording MUST enable routing and add this per-server override:

```json
{
  "mcpNotificationRouting": {
    "enabled": true,
    "perServer": {
      "happy": {
        "resource_updated": {
          "type": "prompt-queue",
          "debounceMs": 250,
          "template": "[agent-comms] you have pending message(s); read the agent-comms MCP resource"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Without this override, the existing default remains `[mcp:happy] resource updated: {uri}`. The pattern doc and integration fixtures must use the override above when asserting the `[agent-comms] ...` prompt.

**Recovery helper + hook** (`agentComms/recovery.ts` + `runCodex.ts` near `:290`, after `MessageQueue2` exists, before event-handler bound) — `agentComms/recovery.ts` exports `recoverPendingAgentCommsMessages<TMode>(sessionId, queue, currentMode)` (plus the shared wake prompt constant). The helper scans the current session's inbox file; if unconsumed entries exist, it pushes a single "[agent-comms] you have pending message(s)" wake prompt through the supplied queue and mode callback, returns whether it enqueued a wake, and does NOT call `markConsumed`. `runCodex.ts` only calls this helper during startup. This is the entire missed-wake recovery — it does NOT replay lost notifications and does NOT inject message bodies into the prompt queue. The message bodies are delivered and consumed only when the receiver performs the explicit MCP resource read/drain described above.

### Implementation Strategy

Ordered for parallel execution where possible (see `## Suggested Decomposition`):

1. **Pattern doc** (`plans/durable-mailbox-channel-wake.md`) — landed early because it's independent of code and serves as the canonical reference the code review can validate against. Supersedes the older `plans/async-events-design.md` (commit 35bc26f6).
2. **Mailbox core module** (`agentComms/mailbox.ts` + colocated `.test.ts`) — foundational; everything else depends on its API surface.
3. **Bridge send tool + producer wake emission**, **daemon route**, **startup recovery helper + hook** — all three depend ONLY on `mailbox.ts` and touch disjoint files (`happyMcpStdioBridge.ts`, `controlServer.ts` + `controlClient.ts`, `agentComms/recovery.ts` + `recovery.test.ts` + `runCodex.ts`). Parallelizable.
4. **Two integration fixtures** in `agentComms/scopeB.test.ts` — depend on all three of step 3 being landed. Single file because the fixtures share setup helpers; the plain `.test.ts` suffix is intentional because `packages/happy-cli/vitest.config.ts` excludes `src/**/*.integration.test.ts` from the unit project and only runs explicitly listed integration files.

- `packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/controlClient.ts` — add `sendAgentMessage(targetSessionId, body, senderSessionId)` helper that posts to the new route using the existing control-client `daemonPost` helper (used by the bridge MCP tool and by lower-level fixtures)
- `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.ts` — startup catch-up wiring:

  - keep recovery behavior out of `runCodex.ts`; this file only supplies the current session id, queue, and mode callback
  - the helper must never call `mailbox.markConsumed`; `MessageQueue2.push()` proves only that a wake prompt was enqueued, not that the receiver drained the durable mailbox
  - message bodies and cursor advancement happen only through the bridge's explicit `agent-comms` resource read/drain callback

## Scope

### In Scope

- The architectural pattern document under `plans/` named "Durable mailbox + channel wake", covering: (1) in-session async events for the U1/U2/U4 subset that benefit from passive notification, (2) `agent-comms` Scopes B + C, (3) codex-as-crews-engine answer. Includes the explicit rejection note for "channels-native crews storage" with rationale.
- ONE reference implementation for `agent-comms` Scope B (same-daemon cross-session messaging) — the smallest implementation that proves the pattern end-to-end.
- Filesystem inbox primitive under `<happyHomeDir>/agent-comms/inboxes/<sessionId>/` with atomic write + history sidecar.
- Daemon-side `POST /agent-comms/send` route serializing cross-session writes through the existing local control plane.
- Codex-facing MCP send tool and producer-side wake emission folded into `happyMcpStdioBridge.ts`.
- Startup catch-up in `runCodex.ts` via an exported `agentComms/recovery.ts` helper, proving the "missed wakes harmless" invariant by mailbox re-read (not by wake replay).
- Two vitest fixtures: happy-path round-trip + missed-wake recovery.
- Calling out `codex-app-server-idle-timeout` interaction in the pattern doc (long-running producer-side MCP servers want app-server to outlive foreground clients) — as an input note to that task's brainstorm, not resolved here.

### Out of Scope

- Building producer infrastructure for U1 (git), U2 (timer), U4 (file-system) generic use cases — those are D-003 "Channels-first Node producer hub", deferred to `async-events-northstar-architecture`.
- Long-poll MCP tool surface (`async_events_wait`) — D-001, deferred to the northstar brainstorm.
- App-server `thread/subscribeEvents` JSON-RPC and its interaction with the codex `fs_watch` crate — D-004, deferred to the northstar brainstorm.
- `agent-comms` Scope A (cross-tunnel / cross-daemon) — stays blocked on the transport-policy decision (relay vs P2P-tunnels vs mobile-broker) that pre-dates channels.
- `agent-comms` Scope C parent-child handshake — pattern is documented as applying to it too, but no reference implementation is built for v1. (The Scope B implementation gives Scope C the same primitives; a follow-up may light up Scope C separately if needed.)
- ANY `codex/` submodule changes. Hard constraint.
- Production-quality multi-producer ecosystem (rate-limiting tiers, per-subscription policy, multi-session per-target routing overrides).
- Cross-machine fan-out of any kind. Channels are intentionally treated as same-daemon only.
- Mid-LLM-call preemption. Delivery is between turns, matching channels + codex mailbox existing semantics.
- Live settings reload (e.g., toggling `mcpNotificationRouting.enabled` at runtime). Recovery is restart-only in v1; live toggle is northstar.
- Mutation of `mcpNotificationConsumer.ts` or `mcpNotificationRouting.ts`. The just-shipped consumer is sufficient and stays unchanged — that's the whole point of D-002 as the cheapest reuse of the consumer.

## Risk Areas

1. **Inbox key collision with codex transport discovery cwdHash.** `codexAppServerClient.ts:1040-1075` keys its WS app-server discovery file by `realpathSync(process.cwd())`. If we keyed the inbox by cwd too, two distinct sessions in the same cwd would collide. **Mitigation:** the inbox is keyed by **session id** (the Happy session id, not the codex thread id), never by cwd. Pin this in `mailbox.ts` JSDoc.
2. **Writer-flush vs reader-poll race.** Atomic-write via temp-file-rename means the read can race the rename window. **Mitigation:** the bridge watches the inbox directory and filters to `mailbox.json` `change`/`rename` events; on a matching event, retry-read once with 50ms backoff; in `mailbox.readPending`, retry-on-`ENOENT`/`EBUSY` up to 3× with backoff. Document the policy in `mailbox.ts` JSDoc.
3. **Debounce coalescing high-frequency wakes.** `resource_updated` defaults to 250ms debounce keyed by `${server}|${uri}` and, without the required `mcpNotificationRouting.perServer.happy.resource_updated` override, renders as `[mcp:happy] resource updated: {uri}`. N rapid messages → 1 wake push. **Mitigation:** the required per-server override's synthesized prompt template MUST say "you have pending message(s)" without a count and direct the reader to read the `agent-comms` MCP resource. The resource read callback picks up ALL N atomically and marks consumed only after returning the entries; debounce coalescing is harmless for the wake-signal pattern. Document this in the pattern doc's configuration section.
4. **Locked inbox during recovery.** A writer holding the file open during a startup scan would fail recovery exactly when it matters. **Mitigation:** atomic-write via rename minimizes lock window to microseconds; retry policy in §2 covers it. Document.
5. **Bridge restart drops `fs.watch` registration.** If the codex client restarts mid-session (force-restart, sandbox forcing), the bridge process is replaced and the new bridge re-registers `fs.watch`. There's a window between old-watch teardown and new-watch arming when writes are not observed — recovered by the startup catch-up reading the inbox before binding the event handler. **Mitigation:** the startup catch-up IS the safety net here; the fixture must explicitly exercise this case.
6. **Sender-side echo / self-wake.** Session A writes to B's inbox; A does NOT wake itself (A's bridge only watches A's inbox). Correct semantics, but a confused tester could expect a self-echo. **Mitigation:** the happy-path fixture explicitly asserts A's `MessageQueue2` receives nothing after A's own send.
7. **Producer-side MCP server lifetime vs `codex-app-server-idle-timeout`.** Long-running consumers want the app-server to outlive the foreground client; the current behavior is bound to a configurable idle timeout. **Mitigation:** out of scope to fix here; surfaced as an input note in the pattern doc and in the follow-up assessment for `codex-app-server-idle-timeout`. Not a blocker for v1.
8. **`writeJsonAtomically` availability under tests.** Test environment must have the `@slopus/happy-wire/node` import path resolvable. Per `packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md`, the wire package exports `writeJsonAtomically` from `node` entry; existing happy-cli tests already use it, so this is a routine integration. **Mitigation:** the mailbox unit test exercises atomic-write via the real helper, not a mock, to keep with the "no mocks as the main proof" policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plans/durable-mailbox-channel-wake.md` exists, names "Durable mailbox + channel wake" as the canonical pattern, lists the three questions it resolves (in-session async events, `agent-comms` B/C, codex-as-crews-engine), contains the explicit rejection note for "channels-native crews storage" with full rationale (loss of cursor / audit / crash-recovery / cross-machine fan-out), includes the `codex-app-server-idle-timeout` interaction note, and documents the required `settings.mcpNotificationRouting.perServer.happy.resource_updated` override that changes the default `[mcp:happy] resource updated: {uri}` prompt into the agent-comms wake prompt.
- [ ] `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/mailbox.ts` exists, exports the documented API (`appendMessage`, `readPending`, `markConsumed`, `inboxPathFor`, `inboxDirFor`, `ensureInbox`), uses `writeJsonAtomically` from `@slopus/happy-wire/node`, and writes both `mailbox.json` and `history.jsonl` under `<happyHomeDir>/agent-comms/inboxes/<sessionId>/`. `ensureInbox(sessionId)` is idempotent and creates the per-session inbox directory plus an empty `mailbox.json` if missing.
- [ ] `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/mailbox.test.ts` passes via `pnpm --filter happy exec vitest run src/agentComms/mailbox.test.ts`, covering append, read-pending, mark-consumed, retry-on-locked-read, and atomic-write under a simulated mid-write process exit.
- [ ] `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/recovery.ts` exports `AGENT_COMMS_WAKE_PROMPT` and `recoverPendingAgentCommsMessages<TMode>(sessionId, queue, currentMode)`. The helper reads pending mailbox entries, pushes exactly one wake prompt when entries exist, returns whether it enqueued a wake, never returns message bodies, and never calls `mailbox.markConsumed`. `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/recovery.test.ts` passes via `pnpm --filter happy exec vitest run src/agentComms/recovery.test.ts`, covering no-op with empty inbox, one wake for one-or-more pending entries, and unchanged cursor after recovery.
- [ ] `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/happyMcpStdioBridge.ts` calls `mailbox.ensureInbox(currentSessionId)` before watcher registration, registers an `agent_comms.send` MCP tool that delegates to `controlClient.sendAgentMessage(targetSessionId, body, currentSessionId)`, registers an `agent-comms` MCP resource at `file:///<absolute-path-to-mailbox.json>`, exposes a resource-read callback that returns pending mailbox entries and only then calls `mailbox.markConsumed(...)`, `fs.watch`es the inbox directory, filters events to `mailbox.json` `change`/`rename`, and calls `server.server.sendResourceUpdated({ uri })` on matching events (debounced ≥ 50ms internally). The watcher is disposed on bridge shutdown, and the watcher / notification path never marks entries consumed.

No code changes to `mcpNotificationConsumer.ts` or `mcpNotificationRouting.ts`.

A calls the `agent_comms.send` MCP tool exposed by A's stdio bridge, which delegates to `sendAgentMessage` targeting B; the daemon writes to B's inbox; B's `mcpNotificationConsumer` (instantiated against a real `MessageQueue2` + `mcpNotificationRouting.perServer.happy.resource_updated` override documented above) receives a `resource_updated` event synthesized as the bridge would; B then reads the `agent-comms` MCP resource on the next turn boundary. A sends a message; B is "shut down" (consumer disposed, simulated process exit). B is "restarted" (routing now enabled, a new consumer + queue), and the fixture invokes `recoverPendingAgentCommsMessages(...)` directly rather than booting `runCodex.ts` or duplicating the recovery logic. Asserts: the helper detects pending mail, pushes ONE wake prompt onto B's queue, and does NOT mark the message consumed; then an explicit `agent-comms` MCP resource read returns the message body and advances the cursor — all WITHOUT any `resource_updated` event being injected. Pin the invariant in the assertion message: "no notification replay occurred; mailbox drain, not wake enqueue, consumed the message."

## Open Questions

These are deliberately documented rather than gated. The implementing member should treat them as decisions to make in-flight and surface to the operator via mailbox messages if the answer materially changes the design:

- **History sidecar format pinning.** v1 uses one JSONL line per entry with `{seq, id, sender, body, ts}` shape. If the team later wants a richer audit format (per-entry signature, encryption envelope), the sidecar can extend without changing the durable `mailbox.json` consumer-facing API. v1 stays simple.
- **`mcpNotificationRouting.perServer["happy"]` shape.** The built-in Happy stdio bridge is registered under the reserved MCP server key `happy`, so the required agent-comms wake-template override belongs at `settings.mcpNotificationRouting.perServer.happy.resource_updated`. v1 leaves the routing code default unchanged; documenting the override path in the pattern doc and fixtures is sufficient.
- **Scope C parent-child reuse.** The pattern doc names Scope C as covered by the same primitive, but no implementation story is included. If the parent-child handshake materially requires Scope-C-specific addressing, file a follow-up; otherwise the same `sendAgentMessage` + inbox model works.
- **Cross-Codex retry on `agent-comms` send.** If the daemon route returns a transient error (e.g., target session evicted), should the bridge-side caller retry? v1 returns the error to the caller and lets the application layer decide; the integration fixture asserts the route returns 404 on missing target, no retry built in.

Add an accept-and-reject case to `mailbox.test.ts`. Implementing member: include this in US-002 if cheap; otherwise file as a fast-follow.

## Northstar forward-compatibility constraints (added post-merge 2026-06-03)

The `async-events-northstar-architecture` brainstorm (commit `950b795b`, selected direction N-001 evolutionary layering) shipped after this plan and surfaced 5 v1 constraints the D-002 implementer MUST bake in to keep v2/v3 forward-compatible. Source: `.ralph/brainstorms/async-events-northstar-architecture/selected-direction.md` lines 80-87.

These are BINDING constraints on this impl (not deferable polish):

1. **Versioned envelope.** Every mailbox entry and wake-notification payload includes a top-level `version: 1` field so future schema evolution (e.g., adding signature / encryption / per-subscription routing) does not require a migration script. Mailbox readers must reject envelopes whose `version` is greater than the consumer's known max with a typed error.
2. **Logical addressing only.** The envelope identifies destination by `sessionId` (logical handle), NOT by physical inbox file path. Filesystem-path-derived routing is an implementation detail of the v1 transport; the wire schema treats addresses opaquely. v2/v3 transports (app-server RPC, cross-machine relay) must be able to route the same envelope shape without filesystem semantics leaking.
3. **Stable URI scheme for wake signals.** The `sendResourceUpdated({ uri })` URI follows a documented scheme like `agent-comms://inbox/<sessionId>` — NOT `file:///<absolute-path>` of the mailbox file. Even though the underlying transport reads from a filesystem mailbox in v1, the URI a consumer sees must be stable when v2/v3 swap the transport.
4. **Per-subscription routing is v2.** v1 ships global-per-server-per-kind routing (matches what `codex-channels-option-b` already established). Per-subscription filters / handlers are a v2 concern. Document in the pattern doc that the v1 routing-config schema reserves the namespace for future per-subscription extension but does NOT implement it.
5. **Between-turns delivery is the v1 contract.** Mid-turn preemption (interrupting a Codex/Copilot session mid-stream to deliver a wake) requires codex-core Rust changes and is explicitly a v3 concern. Document in the pattern doc that v1 wake delivery happens at the next turn boundary; consumers that need finer-grained latency are out of scope.

Implementation impact:
- US-001 (pattern doc) — sections 1, 4, 5 above belong in the pattern document as design rules.
- US-002 (mailbox.ts) — implements 1 (`version` field on every appendMessage) and validates 1 on every readPending.
- US-003 (recovery.ts + bridge) — implements 2 (`sessionId`-keyed addressing only) and 3 (stable URI scheme; use `agent-comms://inbox/${sessionId}` literal, not pathToFileURL).
- Note: F-012 above said "use pathToFileURL for Windows file URIs" — that finding still applies INTERNALLY to any logging/diagnostic file URIs, but the `sendResourceUpdated({ uri })` URI per constraint 3 is NOT a file URI; it's a custom scheme.
